title: Focused Width in Adversarial Fake Detection: A Separation
summary: We study the adversarial fake detection model introduced by Mendelson, Paouris and Vershynin. In this model, a genuine sample is $\pmb{X}\sim N(0,\pmb{I}_n)$, while a fake sample is produced as $\pmb{X}+r\pmb{t}({\pmb{X}})$, where the adversary first observes $\pmb{X}$ and then chooses an admissible perturbation $\pmb{t}({\pmb{X}})$ from a prescribed set $\mathscr{T}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$. The central quantity is the detectability radius $r(\mathscr{T})$, which formalizes the transition scale at which fake samples become reliably distinguishable from genuine ones.
